When sftpEnabled=true (the default configuration in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg), the SSH server exposes the karaf.base directory tree through the MINA SSHD SFTP subsystem and SCP command factory without verifying the authenticated user's roles beyond the initial sshRole login check. Consequently, an authenticated user with only low-privileged roles (such as viewer and ssh) can read sensitive configuration and key files (including etc/users.properties and etc/host.key) or write arbitrary bundles/configurations into monitored directories (such as deploy/ or etc/), leading to privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.


Apache Karaf 4.4.13 and 4.5.0 introduce the sftpRole configuration property in org.apache.karaf.shell (defaulting to admin) and enforce role-based access control on SFTP subsystem creation, SCP command execution, and virtual filesystem access.

Mitigation / WorkaroundUsers are recommended to upgrade to Apache Karaf 4.4.13 or 4.5.0.




On earlier versions where SFTP/SCP access is not required, set sftpEnabled=false in etc/org.apache.karaf.shell.cfg and restart the SSH server bundle (or Karaf instance).

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic in the query construction of AWS Graph Explorer before 3.2.1 might allow an authenticated remote user with write access to the connected graph database to access and modify data in that database with Graph Explorer's privileges via a crafted property key or label that is used when another user performs a search.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to Graph Explorer version 3.2.1 or later.

To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to pgactive version 2.1.10 or later.

ntop n2n supernode 3.0 through 3.1.1 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to leak memory and execute code by sending an untrusted 16-bit auth token_size in REGISTER_SUPER_NAK datagrams. A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

This lets the holder use the account owner's stored third-party credentials, library agents, and workspace files, and run AutoPilot's sandboxed shell, which the same key is refused when it requests those directly. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer.

The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption.

A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size.

Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144).

On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.

Summary

MCUboot enforces several security-critical invariants on the boot, image-swap, and validation paths using assert(). In a standard release/production build (NDEBUG defined) assert() expands to a no-op, so an invariant the code intends to halt on instead falls through, and execution continues with the bad or inconsistent state. Where the guarded condition is attacker-influenceable through the flash-write boundary (serial-recovery / DFU), this is a security check that is simply absent in release builds.

This is one root cause (assert-as-security-guard, no-op under NDEBUG) with one fix approach (replace the security-critical asserts with real fail-closed checks), so it is filed as a single advisory covering the enumerated sites.

Worst reachable instance — inconsistent swap status completes the swap without validation

In the swap-resume status read, an inconsistent status (erased_sections > 1) is detected, logged, and — when MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT is disabled — is meant to abort, because "there is no way to be sure the swapped primary slot is OK." The abort is assert(0):

boot/bootutil/src/swap_move.c:181-194 — if (erased_sections > 1) { ... #if !defined(MCUBOOT_VALIDATE_PRIMARY_SLOT) / ... abort! / assert(0); #endif }, then execution falls through to compute bs->op/idx/state from the inconsistent status (lines 197-208) and return 0 (success).
boot/bootutil/src/swap_offset.c:266-280 — identical pattern; falls through to bs->op/idx/state and return 0.
boot/bootutil/src/swap_scratch.c:227-241 — same invalid/assert(0) pattern for the scratch backend.

Under NDEBUG with primary-slot validation off, the inconsistent status is neither aborted (assert is a no-op) nor re-validated (validation off), so boot_complete_partial_swap() finishes the swap on inconsistent metadata and the primary slot is booted without a signature check. An attacker who can write the swap-status trailer can craft the inconsistent status.

Reachability (threat model). Secondary slot + scratch trailers are A2-writable by definition (that is what a DFU upload is). Under MCUBOOT_SERIAL_RECOVERY the primary trailer is A2-writable too: boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:978 opens flash_area_id_from_multi_image_slot(img_num, 0) (== primary) and writes from offset 0 bounded by area_size, so it can paint the primary swap-status/magic. This is how the A2 (recovery/DFU, unauthenticated by design) attacker influences the guarded condition. Property violated: P1 (image authenticity / secure-boot bypass) when un-revalidated content is booted, and P6 (boot/recovery availability).

Second reachable instance — resume-path swap_size from an unguarded trailer

boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1190-1193: the swap resume branch does fap = boot_find_status(...); assert(fap != NULL); rc = boot_read_swap_size(fap, &bs->swap_size); assert(rc == 0);. boot_find_status() (boot/bootutil/src/bootutil_misc.c:166-204) searches {scratch, primary} and, on no-valid-magic-match, returns the last-iterated area (primary), not NULL — so assert(fap != NULL) cannot fire even in debug, and under NDEBUG neither assert fires. swap_size is then read from an A2-writable (serial-recovery primary, or scratch) trailer with no fail-closed handling. This is the same swap-metadata-trust family as the recorded resume/swap_size disclosure.

4. boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:1191 and :1193 — resume assert(fap != NULL) / assert(rc == 0) guarding swap_size read from an A2-writable trailer; compounded by boot_find_status() never returning NULL.

GNU Inetutils FTP Client File Retrieval Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of GNU Inetutils FTP Client. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must interact with a malicious FTP server.

SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.

SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a reachable assertion in RTCP decoding that lets remote WebRTC peers crash the server. Attackers opening an unauthenticated WHIP or WHEP session can send an 8-byte RTCP packet with undersized length, triggering srs_assert aborts that stop every stream.

Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux contains an origin validation error in the sendMessageToBackend WebKitGTK handler that allows child-frame scripts to invoke the privileged IPC channel. Attackers controlling content loaded in an iframe can post messages that pass the top-level URI origin check and call bound Go methods and Wails runtime operations.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.

Electerm before 5.9.0 contains an origin validation vulnerability in the MCP Server widget that allows remote attackers to execute commands by bypassing Host and Origin checks through DNS rebinding. Attackers can lure users to a page that rebinds to 127.0.0.1 and calls unauthenticated MCP tools on port 30837 to run OS commands locally and on open SSH sessions.

OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection vulnerability in InplaceEditFieldsController via the unvalidated attribute parameter. Webmin through 2.670 contains a signature verification bypass vulnerability in webmin-lib.pl that allows attackers to install unsigned module updates when GnuPG setup fails. Attackers tampering with update downloads via network position or a custom update URL can supply malicious modules that run as root when administrators apply updates.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure download vulnerability in webmin/upgrade.cgi, cluster-webmin/upgrade.cgi and cluster-usermin/upgrade.cgi that fetches upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP with GnuPG signature verification disabled by default. On-path network attackers can substitute a malicious RPM, Debian or tar.gz package during a default upgrade to execute code as root on the Webmin host and managed cluster servers.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the Perl Modules (cpan) module, which downloads CPAN indexes and module archives over plaintext HTTP without checksum or signature verification. On-path network attackers can answer the outbound fetch while an administrator installs a CPAN module, supplying a malicious Makefile.PL that cpan/download.cgi runs as root before confirmation.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing integrity verification vulnerability in usermin/upgrade.cgi that downloads Usermin upgrade packages over plaintext HTTP without signature or digest checks. On-path network attackers or DNS spoofers can supply a malicious RPM, Debian, or tar.gz package whose maintainer scripts or setup.sh execute as root during upgrade.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure default configuration in its Windows setup.bat script that provisions an administrator account with the credentials admin/admin and SSL disabled. Unauthenticated network attackers can log in over plain HTTP on port 10000 with these unchanged credentials to gain full Webmin administrative access.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in fastrpc.cgi that allows unauthenticated network peers to connect to tcpwrite and tcpread file-transfer listeners without session checks. Attackers can race to connect to the predictable transfer port during cluster operations to steal transferred files or replace staged packages, achieving root code execution.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a path traversal vulnerability in minecraft/minecraft-lib.pl that allows unauthenticated game players to overwrite arbitrary files as root via crafted chat messages. Attackers can send chat messages mimicking logged in lines so the root check_playtime_limits cron job rewrites attacker-chosen files, destroying their contents.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in web-lib-funcs.pl and fastrpc.cgi that sends cluster RPC traffic over raw TCP despite SSL configuration. Network-positioned attackers can read the session ID and remote_eval payloads or alter calls in transit to execute code as root on managed servers.

HortusFox (hortusfox-web) through 6.4 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability in UserModel::restorePassword that builds reset links from the client-controlled Host header. Unauthenticated attackers can request a reset with a forged Host header to capture the victim's reset token and take over accounts including administrators.

FCEUX before 2.8.0 contains an integer overflow in SetBoardName() in src/unif.cpp that allows crafted UNIF ROM files to write past a heap buffer. Attackers can persuade users to open a .unf file with a 0xFFFFFFFF MAPR chunk length, wrapping the allocation to zero and corrupting heap memory to crash the emulator or execute code.

FCEUX 2.5.0 before 2.8.0 contains an integer overflow in iNESLoad() in src/ines.cpp that allows a crafted NES 2.0 ROM to write past a heap buffer. Attackers can persuade users to open a .nes file using exponent-multiplier PRG ROM size notation with mappers 53, 198, 228 or 547 to corrupt memory, crashing the emulator and possibly executing code.

OneDev before 17.2.4 contains an argument injection vulnerability in commit query handling that allows authenticated attackers to inject git options through branch or tag names. Attackers can push a branch named like --output=<path> and query it via the commits page or REST API to overwrite server-writable files, causing denial of service.

PyBioNetGen 0.8.7 contains a code injection vulnerability in ParameterBlock.add_item() and ModelBlock.add_item() that allows attackers to execute Python code by passing parameter expressions to sympy.sympify(). Attackers can supply a crafted BNG-XML model file with Python code in a Parameter expr or value attribute to execute code as the user when loaded with bionetgen.bngmodel().

asar-py before 0.1.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in AsarArchive.extract() and extract_archive() that allows attackers to write files outside the destination directory via crafted archive headers. Attackers can supply a .asar archive with '..' path components or malicious symlink targets to write files such as usercustomize.py, leading to code execution.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in the report module (openimis-be-report_py) where the /api/report/reportbro/preview endpoint evaluates printIf expressions server-side using simpleeval with an insufficient name-prefix blocklist. An attacker can craft an expression that reaches sys.modules['os'] via datetime.sys to execute arbitrary operating-system commands as root, and can also exploit the same endpoint's key parameter for unauthenticated arbitrary file read, enabling full host compromise including exposure of database credentials and JWT signing keys.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the OpenSearch reporting dashboard proxy, where the nginx auth_request only verifies login status without checking the declared right before attaching a hardcoded administrative credential to the proxied request, and the backend OpenSearch cluster has its security plugin disabled via a hardcoded compose setting. Any authenticated account, including self-registered or zero-rights users, can exploit this flaw to gain read, write, and delete access to the OpenSearch cluster.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the core export mixin (openimis-be-core_py, core/gql/export_mixin.py) that allows authenticated users with a single ordinary read right to traverse arbitrary foreign key relations by supplying caller-controlled dotted field paths that are rewritten into Django ORM syntax without an allow-list. Attackers can exploit this to export another user's JWT signing key via a path such as user_created.i_user.private_key, enabling them to forge valid authenticated sessions for other accounts, including administrators, without detection through failed-login events or invalidation by password reset.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains an improper validation vulnerability in the deduplication service (openimis-be-deduplication_py, deduplication/services.py) that allows a caller holding only the narrow right 170001 to bypass column path validation by exploiting the fact that only the first segment of a dotted relation path is checked before the full unvalidated path is used in the query. Attackers can supply a crafted dotted column path such as user_created__i_user__private_key to traverse relations and retrieve an administrator's JWT signing key, enabling forgery of a valid administrator session without a password that survives password resets and generates no failed-login event.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a remote code execution vulnerability in the report module's overrideReport GraphQL mutation, which stores submitted report definitions without proper validation before rendering them with the simpleeval expression evaluator. An attacker holding only limited report add, edit, or query privileges can craft a printIf expression that leverages the datetime module to reach os.system functions, bypassing the name-prefix blocklist to execute arbitrary operating-system commands as root whenever the malicious report is later rendered by any viewer, including administrators or scheduled jobs.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a broken access control vulnerability in the FHIR R4 module that allows any authenticated attacker to delete Coverage policy records due to an empty permissions_delete list being vacuously granted by user.has_perms([]). Attackers can issue a DELETE request to the Coverage/<uuid>/ endpoint to permanently and irrecoverably remove insurance policy records.

C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to open a malicious project file delivered through common distribution channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the CertificateSigningRequest controller that allows attackers with permission to create CertificateSigningRequest objects to escalate privileges by exploiting automatic approval of requests carrying a kubesphere.io/username label without verifying the requester's identity or subject match. Attackers can submit a CertificateSigningRequest for the kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client signer with an arbitrary subject such as a platform administrator to obtain a cluster CA-signed client certificate, enabling authentication as the chosen identity and full cluster administrator privilege escalation.

A flaw was found in librelp. When configured to use Transport Layer Security (TLS) with certificate validation and the GnuTLS driver, the library fails to verify the peer certificate chain. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by presenting an invalid or self-signed certificate, allowing them to bypass authentication and act as a trusted log source or collector.

An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework before sending read, update, and delete operations to the database. As a result, a filter that an application relies on to limit which records a request may touch can be omitted silently. A user with basic application privileges may be able to read or change records that the application intended to keep out of reach.

A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a relationship link and the code that searches for one. An application that relies on a relationship-absence query to restrict which records a request may see or change can therefore have that restriction silently fail, allowing a user with basic application privileges to read and to modify or remove records the restriction was meant to cover.

A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be interpreted by the database as query expressions rather than stored as plain text. An application that passes externally supplied data into these helpers may write unintended values into stored documents and may result in unintended disclosure of other data held on the same document. No credentials are required of the party supplying the value.

The MongoDB C Driver does not confirm that the party signing a supplied certificate revocation status response is authorized to answer for the certificate being checked. An unauthenticated party that operates the TLS endpoint a client connects to can therefore have a withdrawn certificate accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of the application's database traffic and in the loss of the revocation decision.

A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted JIF image file, a 32-bit integer overflow occurs during the pixel buffer size calculation, while the zlib output limit is computed separately without wrapping. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the compressed image data is decompressed. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

Sandbox protection in Jenkins Pipeline: Groovy Plugin 4403.v471713a_cea_19 and earlier can be circumvented through interface field initializers, allowing attackers with permission to define and run sandboxed Pipelines to bypass the sandbox protection and execute arbitrary code in the context of the Jenkins controller JVM.

Jenkins Script Security Plugin 1436.v1082791135e4 and earlier does not reject @Builder annotations whose builderStrategy member names an arbitrary class when the annotation is referred to using a partially qualified class name, allowing attackers with permission to define and run sandboxed scripts, including Pipelines, to execute code outside the sandbox if a suitable class is present on the classpath of the component that evaluates the script.

Jenkins Gradle Plugin 2.21.1282.v024680ce00a_b_ and earlier does not configure its XML parser to prevent XML external entity (XXE) attacks when processing Maven extension configuration files from build workspaces.

Jenkins Warnings Plugin 13.10251.va_452d3553728 through 13.10365.v85cd7a_c8110b_ (both inclusive) allows defining inline Groovy parsers whose Groovy scripts are compiled on the Jenkins controller without sandbox protection, allowing attackers able to define inline Groovy parsers to execute arbitrary code in the context of the Jenkins controller JVM.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a command injection vulnerability in the terminal v1alpha2 file download endpoint where the path query parameter is inserted via fmt.Sprintf into sh -c tar commands executed inside the target container, and the DownloadFile handler fails to perform its own pods/exec authorization check. Attackers with only pod get permission, including built-in read-only project-viewer, workspace-viewer and cluster-viewer roles, can supply shell metacharacters in the path parameter to execute arbitrary commands inside any viewable container without holding pod exec permission.

A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently discarded when it is combined into a query. A user with basic application privileges who sends an ordinary request may read, change, or remove records that the restriction was intended to withhold.

An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network endpoint a client connects to, and that holds a revoked but still-dated certificate trusted by that client, to have the connection accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of application credentials and other session data, and in the client treating responses from that endpoint as genuine.

A type-confusion weakness in the Extended JSON parsing component of BSON for Ruby allows a party who can supply parser input to influence how a serialized document is framed. Content placed in one value may be read back as additional or replacement document fields. An unauthenticated party supplying input to an application that parses untrusted Extended JSON and stores the result may cause unintended modification of stored data.

An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a simple identifier value to be turned into an object that is treated as an already-stored record of a caller-chosen model class. In applications that pass unfiltered request data into the affected association handling, an unauthenticated party may cause unintended modification or removal of stored records, and may render an individual record unreadable through that association.

An out-of-bounds read in the native C BSON decoding extension of the MongoDB Python Driver may allow an unauthenticated party who can supply crafted BSON data to the decoder to cause the application process to terminate. In some configurations, nearby process memory may be included in error messages, which may result in limited unintended disclosure of data.

executive_summary: Our environment faces significant exposure across 169 high-severity vulnerabilities, with critical concerns centered on Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) and Apache Karaf. Two AEM code injection flaws score 9.9 CVSS, enabling arbitrary code execution by low-privileged attackers. Additionally, 14 new CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) were added in the past seven days, signaling active threat actor exploitation across the broader ecosystem. Immediate remediation prioritization is essential to protect business continuity, sensitive data, and regulatory standing.
action_items: Immediately patch or mitigate the two CVSS 9.9 AEM code injection vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123266 and CVE-2026-132877) to eliminate arbitrary code execution risk.
Disable or restrict SFTP access on Apache Karaf (CVE-2026-129959) by setting sftpEnabled=false unless explicitly required for business operations.
Assess all 14 newly added CISA KEV entries, particularly HPE Juniper and Drupal Core, and apply available patches within 24-48 hours per federal guidance.
Remediate remaining high-severity AEM vulnerabilities including stored XSS and template injection flaws to prevent privilege escalation and session hijacking.
Implement compensating controls such as web application firewall rules and enhanced privilege monitoring while long-term patching cycles are completed.
risk_narrative: The current threat landscape presents compounding risk from exploitable vulnerabilities across widely deployed enterprise platforms. AEM code injection flaws offer attackers a low-barrier path to full system compromise. The 14 new KEV additions confirm that threat actors are actively weaponizing similar vulnerabilities in production environments. Exploitation of these flaws could result in data exfiltration, ransomware deployment, regulatory penalties, and reputational damage. Organizations using Drupal, HPE Juniper, and Optimizely products face imminent risk given confirmed active exploitation. Without rapid remediation, the attack surface remains critically exposed.
